html:
SMTO-EXE-0125 — The browser step was stopped

GUID: 12da2b24-2dc4-5960-a282-6e2dd2d576a1
Slug: browser-operation-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The browser step was stopped, usually because the task was stopped or the Gateway was shutting down. If the step had already started, it may have changed the page or website.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you pressed Stop on purpose and don't need this step, you don't need to do anything else. Stopping is expected to end the browser step.
  2. Otherwise, ask SMTO to look at its browser and say which page it is on, without clicking anything. The step may have finished just before it was stopped, so the page might already show the result.
  3. Check on the website itself whether the action happened, such as whether the form was sent or the item was saved. Repeating an action that already happened could send or buy something twice.
  4. Only if it did not happen, ask SMTO in a new message to do that step again. Once you know it didn't happen, asking again is safe.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed whether the step happened, and it is done exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, mentioning whether you pressed Stop or the Gateway was restarted. Don't repeat form submissions or payments until you've checked the website.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A browser operation was cancelled before dispatch, while queued, or during execution (for example a user stop or Gateway shutdown); effect_unknown is true only if the action had already started.

What this means

  • Cancellation was recorded before dispatch, observed while waiting for serialized work, or detected after the browser effect boundary; the receipt's effect_unknown flag preserves that distinction. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Cancellation was recorded before dispatch, observed while waiting for serialized work, or detected after the browser effect boundary; the receipt's effect_unknown flag preserves that distinction.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original execution ID, cancellation receipt and current page/download state appropriate to that action.

How to fix it

  • BrowserService.execute/_execute return operation_cancelled when the execution's cancel event is set (BrowserService.cancel or close on Gateway shutdown). A pre-dispatch cancel proves non-execution; after mark() the receipt has effect_unknown=true. Check effect_unknown, then inspect browser.page_info, browser.snapshot and browser.downloads before repeating any write.
  • Inspect the receipt effect_unknown flag. Reconcile page_info/snapshot/downloads before repeating any action that may have executed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the receipt effect_unknown flag. Reconcile page_info/snapshot/downloads before repeating any action that may have executed.

How to verify the fix

  • The original effect is reconciled before any repeated mutation or form submission.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
